name: Kaku SEO
author: kakuapp

sections.description:
Kaku is an AI SEO service for WordPress sites. This plugin connects your site to your Kaku account, so the agent can work on it without copying and pasting.

With your site connected, the agent:

  • Plans and writes articles on the topics that can bring you visits, and publishes them on the days you choose as native Gutenberg blocks that take your theme’s styles.
  • Keeps old posts current: proposes updates to outdated facts and fills content gaps, with every change reviewable before it is published.
  • Writes SEO titles and meta descriptions into Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress.
  • Improves internal linking: links related posts to each other and fixes broken links.
  • Optimizes images: writes alt text in every language of your site and compresses oversized images.
  • Optimizes WooCommerce products: titles, descriptions, meta tags and an FAQ tab, which you review before they are published.
  • Writes in more languages, with its own articles for each one, with Polylang or WPML.

Kaku also gives your site a weekly health score and shows your Google Search Console traffic.

How it works

The agent works from Kaku: it decides what to do first by the visits each task can bring, and this plugin applies its work on your site. New articles on your schedule, missing meta tags and alt text, image compression, internal links and broken-link fixes are applied directly. Refreshed posts and WooCommerce products wait for you to review them in Kaku. A broken link the agent cannot fix without changing what the sentence says is left as it is.

You can choose which kinds of work the agent does, have new articles saved as drafts instead of published, let it apply everything without review, or pause it at any time.

Requirements

The plugin needs a Kaku account and a plan for the site. Each site starts with a 7-day trial in its main language, and each extra language is an add-on. See the plans at kaku-app.site.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Kaku (https://kaku-app.pro), the hosted service that provides all of its features. It does not contact Kaku until you connect the site.

When you connect the site (by clicking “Connect to Kaku”, by activating a copy of the plugin downloaded from your Kaku account, which carries your site’s connection code, or by approving Kaku’s connection request on your WordPress authorization screen), the plugin sends Kaku:

  • the site’s address and the plugin version (with the “Connect to Kaku” button, also the site’s name);
  • technical details of the installation: the WordPress, PHP and database versions, and the web server and its limits;
  • which page builder, SEO, multilingual, security and e-commerce plugins are active;
  • the site’s languages, post categories and tags.

While the site is connected, the plugin:

  • tells Kaku when one of those plugins is activated or deactivated, when the site’s languages, categories or tags change, when this plugin is updated, deactivated or disconnected, and when a post, page or product is deleted or moved to the trash;
  • talks to Kaku with a connection key that belongs to this site alone, which Kaku can replace with a new one;
  • lets Kaku read, through authenticated requests, the posts, pages, products and images the agent works on, and write back its work: the changes it applies directly and the ones you approve. Kaku can only work on that content, and move to the trash the articles it published; it cannot change your settings, users, plugins or themes;
  • lets Kaku read again the technical details listed above when it needs them;
  • saves Kaku’s changes without signing in as any user, so WordPress filters them as it filters the changes of a user who cannot post unfiltered HTML. If a post contains HTML that this filter would remove, such as an embed or a script, the plugin leaves that post unchanged;
  • receives the images of the articles Kaku publishes together with each article, checks that they are images, and adds them to the media library. It does not download images from Kaku or from any other site;
  • forgets its connection when you remove the site from your Kaku account. The plugin stays active until you deactivate it.

Kaku is provided by Axis Software Solutions SL. Terms of use · Privacy policy

YouTube. Articles can include a YouTube video, inserted with WordPress’s own embed block. When a visitor views the article, the video player loads from YouTube. YouTube terms of service · Google privacy policy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins → Add New and activate it.
  2. Open Kaku in the WordPress admin menu and click Connect to Kaku.
  3. Sign in to Kaku, or create an account, and confirm the site. You will come back to WordPress with the site connected.

You can also download the plugin from your Kaku dashboard when you add a site. That copy carries the site’s connection code and connects as soon as you activate it.

Or connect in one click from your Kaku dashboard: WordPress asks you to approve Kaku as an application, and Kaku installs this plugin from WordPress.org, activates it and connects it. Kaku uses the application password WordPress creates for that approval only to do this, and deletes it from your site when it is done. It needs an administrator account and a site served over HTTPS.

Kaku works with WordPress installed at the root of its domain (example.com), not in a folder such as example.com/blog.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Kaku account?

Yes. The plugin connects your site to Kaku, where the agent runs. You can create an account while connecting. Each site needs a plan, which starts with a 7-day trial.

Will Kaku change my site on its own?

Only the work you leave to the agent. It publishes new articles on your schedule and applies meta tags, alt text, image compression, internal links and broken-link fixes directly. Refreshed posts and WooCommerce products wait for your review. In Kaku you can turn each kind of work off, have articles saved as drafts or pause the agent. Kaku only works on your content: it never changes your settings, users, plugins or themes.

Which SEO plugins does it work with?

Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO and SEOPress. Meta tags are written into the SEO plugin you already use.

Does it work with my page builder?

Articles are published as standard Gutenberg blocks, so they follow your theme’s post template whatever builder the rest of the site uses. Post refreshes work on posts built with the block editor, the classic editor or Elementor.

Is AI-generated content marked?

Yes. Posts and images created or rewritten by Kaku carry a machine-readable label on their page, following the EU AI Act.

How do I update the plugin?

Like any other plugin from WordPress.org: from your plugin list, or automatically if you turn on auto-updates for it. When Kaku needs a newer version than the one installed, your Kaku dashboard tells you.

How do I disconnect the site, or connect it to another Kaku account?

Open the Kaku page in your WordPress admin and click Disconnect. You can then connect it again, to the same account or another one, with Connect to Kaku.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating it disconnects the site from Kaku; activating it again reconnects it. Deleting it removes its settings from your database. Content already published stays on your site.
sections.changelog:
2.52.0

  • Wording updates on the Kaku page of your dashboard and in the plugin description.

2.51.0

  • The images of an article Kaku publishes reach the media library with their alt text, including the featured image. An image that already had an alt text on your site keeps it.

2.50.0

  • Fixed: Kaku did not learn that the site uses an SEO plugin activated at the same time as Kaku, so it did not write SEO titles and descriptions. The plugin now checks the active plugins and tells Kaku about any change from the dashboard.
  • Fixed: on a page whose address contains accented or non-Latin characters, Kaku could not find the page, so it left its broken links and its internal links untouched and reported them as missing from the page.
  • When Kaku removes a broken link whose text only existed to be a link, it can rewrite the sentence so the page still reads well. It only ever rewrites text that contains the broken link, it never adds a link that was not already there, and it leaves the page untouched if the text has changed since Kaku read it.

2.49.0

  • Kaku’s changes to your content are saved without signing in as any user, so WordPress filters them like those of a user who cannot post unfiltered HTML. A post with HTML that this filter would remove is left unchanged.
  • Kaku can no longer update or deactivate the plugin: it is updated from your plugin list like any other, and removing the site from Kaku only disconnects it.
  • Kaku only moves to the trash the articles it published.
  • The technical details Kaku reads include the plugin version.

2.48.0

  • Each site talks to Kaku with a connection key of its own, and Kaku can replace it with a new one.
  • Changes to categories, tags and languages reach Kaku even if it was unavailable when they happened, and deleting a category or tag is reported too.
  • The admin no longer checks categories, tags and languages on every background request.
  • Connecting in one click checks the new connection before replacing a working one.
  • Internal links and broken-link fixes on Elementor posts refresh the page caches, and are written to the post content when Elementor is not active.
  • An internal link to an address with a dollar sign keeps its address intact.
  • FAQ structured data follows the questions the post shows today, without HTML entities, and is not printed on password-protected posts.
  • Product listings include every language in WPML and Polylang.
  • Placeholder images without an address are not published.
  • Image compression keeps each image’s format and file names, so images already in your posts keep working; it starts from the file your site serves, respects edits made in WordPress and the photo’s orientation, and never replaces an image with a heavier one.
  • Animated PNG images are left as they are, like animated GIF and WebP.
  • Compressed images also update their copies in other languages, and alt text is written only for the site’s active languages without unlinking existing translations.

2.47.0

  • Kaku’s changes to your content are saved as the administrator who connected the site, so WordPress and Elementor apply the same content rules as when that person edits it.
  • The images that come with an article are checked to be images before they are added to the media library, and an article whose images cannot be added is not published.
  • The Update plugin button in Kaku uses the same update process as Update now in your plugin list.
  • Notifying Kaku that a post was deleted or that categories or tags changed no longer makes WordPress wait for Kaku’s reply.
  • Removed the post translation and category and tag creation endpoints, which Kaku no longer uses.

2.46.0

  • Articles can carry a table of contents, tables, an FAQ section, a YouTube video, a call to action and a fixed notice, all as native blocks.
  • The article arrives with its excerpt, its SEO title and description, and in its language in Polylang or WPML.
  • FAQ structured data on articles with an FAQ section, and Article structured data on sites without an SEO plugin.

2.45.0

  • The Kaku page presents Kaku. Once the site is connected, it opens the agent’s screens on this site: overview, content calendar, improvements, site health and agent settings.

2.44.0

  • Connect or disconnect your site from the new Kaku page in the WordPress admin. Before connecting, it shows what Kaku does; once connected, it opens each tool on this site.
  • Connect in one click from your Kaku dashboard, after approving Kaku in WordPress.
  • Updates are delivered through WordPress.org.
